items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like encodeIndexShape and decodeIndexLoop are clear, and the format layout comment is good. But the business logic relies on single-letter names: `p := &Polygon{}`, `l := &Loop{...}`, `g := &genericShape{}`, `c := &clippedShape{...}`, `sh`. The cap limits this to accept.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `func (s *ShapeIndex) decode` runs about 140 lines with nested cell, clipped-shape and edge loops, which exceeds the 100-line cap. The new shapeindex_encode.go is 614 lines. It ignores the convention to put per-shape encode/decode next to each type (lax_*.go, loop.go) and puts every shape's codec in one file.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every count is bounded (readCount, maxEncodedCells) and preallocation is capped with `min(n, maxDecodePrealloc)`. Shape IDs, CellID order and overlap, and edge ranges are validated. EOF is mapped to ErrUnexpectedEOF. State is swapped under the lock only after a full decode succeeds. Truncation, corruption and fuzz runs produce no panics.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: Adds only Encode/Decode on ShapeIndex. Existing per-shape wire formats and typeTag values are untouched, and the Shape interface is unchanged. The new index-local tags (shapeIndexTagLoop=6, LaxLoop=7, Generic=8) renumber nothing. The shapeindex.go edits are internal fixes and do not affect any format.
